claim: Quant is not a new blockchain: it is the layer in the middle of what banks already run, seven named UK banks are already on it, and against its peers it is the one line that left the group.
why_this_claim: It is the longform's own thesis (the title's 'the layer the banks let in') told without the whiteboard story, so it needs none of the islands set-up. It holds cold because each piece is something the viewer can see: the diagram shows where Quant sits, the receipt lists the banks, the chart shows one orange line above the rest. It makes no price call and no promise about the future. The only live-drift figure is 273, and the chart prints its index date.

assembled_read: So what is quant? And what they sell is not a new blockchain. On the left, what a bank already runs. Core Banking, Treasury, the payment rails. In the middle, Quant. So who's actually using this? Seven banks are on it. Barclays, HSBC, Loy's, Monzo, Nationwide, NatWest and Santander. And then one line leaves the group. A year later, quant sits at 273. And every other line in this chart is below 100.

rejected.reason: The layer line, 'And then the big one, the clearing house', the 25 islands, 'a layer the banks are actually letting into the building' and the landing line. The best words in the video, all on whiteboard windows, so rule 8 removes them.

'The US payments company owned by 25 of the largest US banks. It runs RTP and chips and clears more than $2 trillion a day.' The biggest receipt, but its name is spoken on WB6, and 'they picked' (300.98) and 'first half of 2027' (308.98, WB7) cannot come with it. Without those lines the short would imply the 2 trillion dollars already runs on Quant, which the screenplay's WARNING forbids.

The only sentence stating The Clearing House selected Quant carries the 'they picked bank' misspeak (PROJECT-LOG, left as recorded). The longform covers it with TCH's printed text in the deck area, but in the short's FACE crop that text is out of frame.

'GBTD, that's the Great British Tokenized Deposit Platform. Run by UK Finance and Quant built the infrastructure for it.' The precise version of span 5, and my first choice for accuracy. Its first 4 s sit on the CLIP-1 lead-out, a held video frame with a burned caption typed 'container', with no slide source for slide-builder to rebuild. Starting at 'Run by' instead would follow 'In the middle, Quant' and read as Quant being run by UK Finance.

CLIP-1, Verdian's own voice. A strong line, but it is a 16:9 third-party clip with a burned caption, its cover_type is outside VCARD_KINDS so no native rebuild exists, and the coverage gate would fail it.

'For 10 months, quant didn't do anything special.' The ideal set-up for the kicker. It would be a second span on the same C6 beat, and s_vertical_cards records only the first hit per id, so its window would stay uncovered and fail s_verify_final. See risks for how to get it back.
'And this is all the while its peers fell from 40 to 60%.' Would extend the kicker cleanly, but takes the total to about 30 s of spans.

'So Chainlink, Hedera, XRP, Styler, Canton, everything indexed to 100 on November 5th, 2025.' A clean FACE span that names the peers. At 6.38 s it would have to replace span 3, which carries the 'layer' half of the claim, and the chart already prints the names and date. A good swap if Mike prefers a coins-forward short.

C5: 'the clearing house news, and the share goes from 0.028 to around 0.09% in 10 weeks, more than a three X.' 'The share' has no referent cold, it takes 11 s, and a second chart dilutes the one idea.
C7: '3.5 X against Bitcoin in a year.' A live-drift ratio the screenplay only airs with both dates, and a second chart.
Bank of England lab and ECB receipts. A test and a pioneer listing are weaker than seven named banks on a platform Quant built, and 12 s is too long.
The full opening down to 'I should buy some quant.' A real hook, but it holds no claim and costs 8.5 s more, which would force out the diagram or the banks.
'Quant is a London company founded in 2015 by a guy named Gilbert Veridian.' Clean edges, but it is a spec line that adds 5.2 s and moves nothing forward.
F5 price, market cap and rank: live-drift numbers, wrong by the time the short posts, with burns on both edges.

risks: RULE 2 EXCEPTIONS (spans 2 and 4), Mike's call. Both FACE spans have a visible film burn at their outer edge because the words themselves sit inside the burn. I pulled frames from quant-FINAL.mp4: the face stays legible and nothing is half-melted, and both burns land on a join where v1 added its own burn hit. Stacked, those two can blow out for a frame or two, so the builder may want to drop the added hit on these two joins. I have not seen this assembled.

STRICT FALLBACK with no visible burn: 'So what is quant?' (0.00-1.35) + 'Right, so here's the short version.' (20.485-22.60) + span 3 + span 5 + the kicker started at 468.52 ('And this is all the while its peers fell from 40 to 60%...'), about 27.3 s. It stays fully clear of transitions but loses 'not a new blockchain' and 'who's actually using this', which is why it is not the main plan. To drop only span 4's burn, remove it and put 20.485-22.60 before span 2 (about 27.0 s), though that makes three spans from F1 in a row.

ACCURACY, 'Seven banks are on it.' In the longform 'it' is GBTD. Here it points at Quant. The capture supports the link (the banks are on the GBTD platform 'developed by Quant'), but UK Finance convened it and calls this 'retail live pilots'. The short never says 'live' or 'in production', yet it is a looser claim than Mike's own line, and this is the main thing to overrule. The precise wording is unavailable: see the 250.26-258.04 rejection.

IMPLIED CAUSE. Banks then a breakout chart suggests the banks caused the move. Nothing spoken says so. The longform ties the move to The Clearing House news, which this short does not name, and that is the open loop into the full video. 273 is a snapshot from 2026-11-04, printed on the chart with its index date.

NATIVE REBUILDS DO NOT EXIST YET, and a card that fails visual-qa twice fails the node. C1: the VO says 'on the left' and 'in the middle', so the bank stack must stay physically LEFT of the Quant block, not stacked above it, and both must be lit in the one still. C14: the bank list and 'developed by Quant' are far apart on the page, so one screen may not show both; the bank list comes first. C6: must use the payoff state and keep the index date. The builders receive only COVER-PLAN's 'what' text, not this plan, so the orchestrator should pass these three notes on. v1's QA also found native receipts must be shown flat, with no push, to pass the edge-text gate.

F3 STRIP MASK. v1's QuantShort.tsx masks the deck-area sliver by hand, measured on F1 only. In F3 that sliver shows the C20 headshot (visible in my crop tiles), so the mask needs re-measuring for span 4 or a cropped asset will show beside the strip.

PIPELINE TRAP FOUND. s_vertical_cards dedupes hits by id and records one overlay_short per id, so two spans on the same cover beat leave the second uncovered. This plan avoids it with one span per beat. If that is fixed, 'For 10 months, quant didn't do anything special.' can replace span 4, placed before the kicker: 459.20-461.80 for 210.33-211.96, about 27.5 s. I read this in the code and did not test it, and I did not change the code.

COLD READS, from text only. Span 2 opens on 'And', span 6 on 'And then', and span 3 goes straight to 'On the left'. I read them as one breath-run with the pictures carrying them, but I have not heard the seams. Delivery energy is inferred from the screenplay's gear map, not heard.

NARROW CUTS. This is a desilenced spine, so most measured gaps are under the 0.25 s preference (span 4's out is 0.04 s, span 2's out 0.08 s). Every boundary sits at a measured trough, and the lane's 12 ms crossfade applies. Span 4's out is the one to listen to first.
CAPTIONS. 'Loy's' must print as 'Lloyds' and 'quant' as 'Quant'. Both are on AS-RECORDED's mishear list, which s_captions applies; check them on the finished short.
